newsitem.title: LEBANON: Katyusha rockets slam into Israel.
newsitem.headline: Katyusha rockets slam into Israel.

text.p: Katyusha rockets fired from south Lebanon slammed on Wednesday evening into northern Israel and Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

Several rockets slammed into the western Galilee and 12 of the Soviet-made rockets hit an empty area near the town of Markaba in the Israeli-held zone in south Lebanon, the South Lebanon Army (SLA) sources said.

It was the second time Katyusha rockets fired from Lebanon have hit northern Israel since April 27, 1996, when a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding ended a 17-day Israeli blitz against pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon.
In an attack in December at least one rocket hit northern Israel without causing damage or casualties. Lebanese and Lebanon-based Palestinian guerrilla factions had denied any links to it.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for firing the rockets on Wednesday but the attack came hours after a clash in the south Lebanon zone in which one Israeli soldier was killed and four wounded.

Hizbollah (Party of God) is leading a guerrilla war against Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong South Lebanon Army militia holding the 15-km (nine-miles) south Lebanon zone intended to protect northern Israel from cross-frontier raids.
